summary: Fumihiko Sueki works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Yoshiro Tamura, Kyosho Hayashima, and Hajime Nakamura. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo, Nichibunken, and SOKENDAI.

Fumimaro Watanabe worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University and the University of Toronto under Hammalawa Saddhatissa and Anthony Kennedy Warder. He held posts at Kindai University, Pali Text Society, and Aichi Gakuin University.
Fumio Enomoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a research assistant at Kyoto University (circa 1981–1984) and as a professor at Osaka University (circa 1999–2017).

Fumio Masutani worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the Fifth Higher School and the University of Tokyo, later serving as professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and Taisho University, and president of Tsuru University.

Fumio Matsuda works in religious and Buddhist studies. He has held positions at Komazawa University and served as an executive committee chair for the Japanese Association for the Study of Indian Religions in 1997.

Fumio Ouchi specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history and archaeology. He earned his doctorate at Otani University, where he later served as associate professor (circa 1993–2000) and professor (circa 2000–2017).
Fumio Shoji is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Rissho University, where he also served as an assistant professor in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies in 2015.

Fumio Tamamuro specializes in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Meiji University from circa 1954 to 1964 and subsequently held a post there from circa 1966 to 2006.

Futoshi Omae is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as a lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1991) and held a post at Shimane Prefectural Junior College of International Studies (attested 1997).

Futoshi Takehashi is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied in the doctoral program at Otani University (attested 1992). He held an assistant post at the Institute of Shin Buddhist Studies from 1995 to 1997.

Fyodor Buslaev worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the Faculty of History and Philology of Moscow University from circa 1834 to 1838 and obtained a post at Moscow State University in 1846.

Fyodor Shcherbatskoy studied at Saint Petersburg State University and under Georg Bühler, Hermann Jacobi, and Ivan Pavlovich Minaev. A scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, he served as a professor at Saint Petersburg State University (circa 1900–1941).

Félix Nève was an Indologist and linguist who studied at KU Leuven and under Christian Lassen, Friedrich Wilhelm Thiersch, and Eugène Burnouf. He served as a professor at KU Leuven starting in 1841, becoming professor emeritus in 1877.

G. C. Nayak was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He served as a Fellow at the Indian Institute of Advanced Study from circa 1992 to 1994 and as a Senior Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research in 1996.

G. Thomas Tanselle studied at Yale University and taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and Columbia University. He also served as vice president of the John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation and president of the Bibliographical Society of America.

G. V. Aston is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. Aston earned a Doctor of Philosophy in Philosophy at the University of Canterbury between 1986 and 2004, studying under doctoral supervisor Jack Copeland and teacher Paul Harrison.

id: P:Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso
summary: Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso studied under Tenzin Gyatso and Trijang Rinpoche.

Gadjin M. Nagao specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Kyoto University under Ryotai Hatani and Susumu Yamaguchi, later holding the Chair of Buddhist Studies at Kyoto University (1935–1971) and a professorship at Kyushu University.
Gail Hinich Sutherland is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Chicago under Carol Bolon, Wendy Doniger, and Virendra Singh.

Gajanan Balkrishna Palsule worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as a sub-editor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (circa 1955–1968) and held a post at Savitribai Phule Pune University (circa 1968–1981).
